newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS- T-bond vols sag as bonds rally after data.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS- T-bond vols sag as bonds rally after data.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options sagged across the board as the underlying market rallied after friendly economic data, traders said.

Unlike Wednesday's sharp reversal after an early spike up, T-bonds were able to retain most of their early gains fuelled by a modest rise in July consumer price index (CPI), a sign of returning confidence in the market, they noted.
"After all the numbers we had this week, plus no data tomorrow and the weekend coming up, I think people are just discounting (risk premium) here," said a brokerage trader.
Implied volatility for October and December T-bond futures options on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) fell about a quarter point each to around 8.3 and 8.5 percent respectively.
Hardest hit were September options, which expire in about a week on August 22. September volatility fell three quarters of a point to about 8.1 percent.

Traders said interest in Septembers was waning, even though the contract covers next week's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting and has very high gamma, which provides quick premium acceleration and big delta swings against bond price movements that the meeting could induce.

"FOMC, everybody already assumes nothing's going to happen, so there's no anxiety going into that," the brokerage trader said. "We hit those humps (economic data this week) and now we're basically just waiting for next month's payrolls, next month's inflation numbers and next month's FOMC (due on September 30)."

September T-bond futures rallied on news that July CPI was up 0.2 percent, both overall and excluding food and energy, in line with economists' average forecasts. The contract surged past Wednesday's 113-19/32 peak to a high of 113-24/32.

Among the biggest trades in the CBOT bond pit, a bank was seen buying 3,000 contracts of September 114 calls and another firm was said to have sold 2,000 lots of September 112-113 vertical put spread.

The shorter end of the yield curve saw relatively light options activity with volatilities easing slightly. Implied volatilities for December and March Eurodollar futures options stood at 8.5 and 10.6 percent, about 0.2 point each lower.
A brokerage trader said futures appeared to have regained a firm footing on the 94.00 handle, and there was little interest to build up positions ahead of the FOMC meeting.
